picks.title: Harbor of New Haven
picks.why: A Coast Survey harbor map provides an early waterfront baseline.
picks.limitations: One date only; verify shoreline definition, map scale and digitized access.

picks.title: City and vicinity of New Haven, Connecticut, derived wholly from the maps of the U.S. Coast Survey and of the City Engineer Department
picks.provider: James P. Bogart and Horace Andrews,Photo lith. by J. Bien
picks.why: City and Coast Survey sources offer a second nineteenth-century map.
picks.limitations: Confirm that the waterfront is depicted and assess its scale and survey dates.

picks.title: City of New Haven, Connecticut
picks.provider: Published by Geo. H. Walker & Co.
picks.why: A late nineteenth-century city map can fill an intermediate date.
picks.limitations: Waterfront coverage, scale and survey date require inspection.

picks.title: New Haven quadrangle, New Haven County, Connecticut
picks.provider: United States, Department of the Interior, Geological Survey
picks.why: A USGS quadrangle provides a near-endpoint historical map.
picks.limitations: Inspect edition and survey dates and verify shoreline detail and coverage.

picks.title: New Haven
picks.provider: Army Map Service, Corps of Engineers, War Dept,Sold and distributed by U.S. Geological Survey
picks.why: An Army Map Service map offers another near-endpoint source.
picks.limitations: Confirm whether it derives from earlier surveys and whether shoreline detail is adequate.

picks.title: CT ECO (UConn): orthophotos, lidar, land cover
picks.why: Historical aerial imagery can help check waterfront features and map alignment.
picks.limitations: Check New Haven availability and actual image date and resolution; aerial water edges depend on tide.

time.label: partial
time.reason: Covers 1934 to 1950 of your 1850 to 1950 window

resolution.label: unknown
resolution.reason: 50 cm data; set a needed resolution to compare

picks.title: New Haven Roads
picks.why: Modern roads can help locate stable intersections for aligning historical maps.
picks.limitations: Modern roads are not historical evidence; verify each control point persisted.

methods.name: Georeference and digitize historical maps
methods.why: Align each map using stable landmarks, then trace dated shorelines with documented residual errors.
methods.tools: QGIS Georeferencer or ArcGIS Pro; YCGS consultation

methods.name: Compare shoreline positions and uncertainty
methods.why: Overlay dated lines and measure changes only where they exceed alignment and map-scale uncertainty.

next_steps: Inspect each map for harbor coverage, scale, survey date and shoreline or tidal definition.
Locate additional maps around 1850–1867 and 1900–1933 to fill temporal gaps.
Use stable landmarks to align scans and record uncertainty before digitizing.
